reader.requirement: At COBOL-85, when FUNCTION RANDOM's argument-1 is written it must be an integer argument (§1989:A.2.2 AR4; never a numeric function, §1989:A.2.3 GR2), refused at compile time when it is not, with a zero or positive value (a value constraint, undefined on breach per §1989:A.2.2 p3), and it seeds a sequence: the same seed restarts the same sequence (§1989:A.2.35.4 RV2) and the values lie in [0,1).

reader.notes: The seed site (CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs#Random) holds only the value half; the integer half lives in the Verified row Uniform('i') for RANDOM, screened by IntegerViolation, which refused every non-integer seed shape at --std 85. Seeding restarts a deterministic sequence per seed, wide seeds are accepted (low 31 bits, documented), and a negative seed terminates at 85, which §1989:A.2.2 p3 permits.
reader.at-2023: the same refusals; a negative seed raises EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION

refuter.evidence: Seeds: RANDOM(FUNCTION MAX(A B)) runs (intfn.cob); RANDOM(ZERO) runs (r_zero.cob; ZERO is an arithmetic-expression term at 85, §1985:VI.6.2.1); RANDOM(C) and RANDOM(C - 2147483648) for C = 999999999999999998 give the same value (big.cob), which the documented low-31-bit reduction gives and §1989:A.2.35.4 RV3 permits (the distinct-sequence subset need only include 0 through 32767; the reduction is the identity there, CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs#Random). Refusal half: FUNCTION RANDOM as its own seed (r_rndsp.cob), (FUNCTION MEAN(2 4)) in parentheses (p_rnd.cob) refused COBOL1627 §1989:A.2.3. Class c: RANDOM ( ) with an empty list refused COBOL0900 at 85 (r_rndp.cob; 1985's format is [ ( argument-1 ) ]); FUNCTION SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT refused COBOL1502 (c_seconds.cob). cite.py: OK §1989:A.2.35.3 AR1 'it must be zero or a positive integer'; OK §1989:A.2.35.4 RV3 'This subset must include the values from 0 through at least 32767'; OK §1989:A.2.2 AR4; OK §1989:A.2.3 GR2; OK §1985:VI.6.2.1.
